trap-thesis-restatement.evidence: The block-final sentence ('The coordinates q and i govern the structure: q generates radial motion, while i generates the sigma-rotation connecting rays') is a decomposition reading — radial versus angular — not a restatement of anything the block established, so it does not fire this criterion.
trap-thesis-restatement.notes: pass on the trap criterion, but that closing sentence is loose on its own terms: q and i are not coordinates on C^x, and neither 'generates' anything in the group sense — sigma and tau are the generators, and q is the point being acted on. FIVE MATH FINDINGS, none fixed inline. (1) M IS NOT IN GL_2(Z). det [[-1,4],[4,3]] = -3 - 16 = -19, and GL_2(Z) requires det = +-1. The block asserts 'M in GL_2(Z)' and later 'M, M' in GL_2(Z) as the real-axis elements'. Its Moebius action is fine (only the projective class matters) and its FIXED PAIR IS CORRECT — I solved (-z+4)/(4z+3) = z and got exactly {1/phi, -phi} — so only the group-membership claim is wrong. Proposed: GL_2(Q), or PGL_2(Z[1/19]), or drop the ambient group. (2) THE TWO i-ROTATED FIXED PAIRS ARE SWAPPED. The block says M^sigma = S^{-1} M S 'fixes the i-rotated golden pair {i/phi, -i phi}' and that its bar conjugate fixes {i phi, -i/phi}. Solving (-z-4i)/(4iz+3) = z gives iz^2 + z + i = 0, i.e. z^2 - iz + 1 = 0, whose roots are i(1 +- sqrt 5)/2 = {i phi, -i/phi} — the OTHER pair. Two independent confirmations: direct substitution, M^sigma(i phi) = (-i(phi+4))/(3-4phi) = i phi exactly; and the conjugation identity, S^{-1}MS fixes S^{-1}(fix M) = -i{1/phi, -phi} = {-i/phi, i phi}. The pair the block assigns, {i/phi, -i phi}, is S(fix M), which is fixed by S M S^{-1}, the conjugate in the other direction. Proposed: swap the two sentences, or redefine M^sigma := S M S^{-1}. (3) M' IS NEVER DEFINED. It appears only in '{M, M', M^sigma, M'^sigma}' and 'M, M' in GL_2(Z)'. (4) 'Each matrix fixes exactly one coset of G_8' does not add up: each of the four matrices fixes a PAIR, so four matrices account for 8 = |G_8| points, whereas a coset of <sigma> in G_8 has 4 elements and four cosets would be 16. Proposed: 'Each matrix fixes exactly one antipodal pair'. (5) 'FIXED LOCUS' IS THE WRONG WORD, and the sentence is self-contradicting: 'Together, G_8 union {zeta_8-orbit} form the full D_4-fixed locus on C^x' — these are orbits, not fixed points (the stabilisers are trivial for G_8 and order 2 for the zeta_8 orbit), they do not exhaust C^x (D_4 acts on every point of C^x), and the table immediately below lists two further orbit types, so the union of two of the four is not 'the full' anything. The table's last row also puts 0 and infinity in a locus the header restricts to C^x, from which 0 is excluded by definition.
